HEEWON WEBTOON — a KOREAN WEBTOON character-introduction splash used as a movie still, bold manhwa cover finish (Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader). A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (medium close, two-shot, three-shot, split) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, dutch), never a flat catalogue pose, never a photoreal landscape with tiny people. LINE: THICK, confident black ink contours with real line weight — a heavy tapered outline around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands; solid black spot-blacks fill the deepest shadows, the hair masses and the insides of sleeves. SHADING: cel-shaded in hard-edged shapes — a base tone, ONE crisp shadow shape and one small sharp highlight per surface, at most one soft gradient for form; glossy graphic highlights on hair, eyes, lacquer and steel. Clean saturated colour. NOT painterly brushwork, NOT watercolor, NOT soft sketchy lines, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. CHARACTER DESIGN: a DESIGNED character, never a generic handsome manhwa face — the face shape, eye shape, brows, nose, mouth, build and posture below belong to this person and no one else, pushed far enough that they read at thumbnail size and in silhouette alone. KOREAN FACES: these are 7th-century Koreans, drawn the way the best Korean webtoons draw Koreans — living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black), East Asian bone structure, single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, a low soft Korean nasal bridge (never a high European nose), broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair; varied from person to person (moon faces, long faces, square jaws), never Western, Latin or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes, never the interchangeable pretty anime face. Keep identity from the attached sheet (hair, dress, colours, ornaments) but REDRAW the person in this bolder style; the sheet's soft sketchy rendering is not the style. OVERRIDE: if a note says photoreal-numinous, IGNORE it — REDRAW every face as webtoon ink. The attached portraits of Big Star and Little Star are photographs of actors: copy hair colour, clothes colours and bone structure ONLY. NEVER photographic skin, pores, live-action lighting, or camera grain. Faces LARGE in the central band. INTRO-CARD WEBTOON three-shot, faces LARGE. DAY. Over-shoulder from the wall-walk. ONE DEVICE: the stone parapet as a hard horizontal; the north-west road a pale diagonal below. LEFT = Namsan in the helm with the RED plume and gold brow-disc, leaning to whisper, wrecked eyes. SECOND = Namgun, LONG hair, no helm, staring down, mouth already opening on a shout. THIRD = Namseng SMALL on a horse on the road in a TANG VERMILION court coat — NOT Goguryeo red-wing lamellar, NOT the red scarf, the Western coat is the point. One of each. NEVER clone. NEVER put the Tang coat on Namgun. Pyongyang's red munru a graphic stamp. #d4776a / #9e3b32 / #c25a4e as real light. Thick ink. Not photoreal. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = namsan, SECOND face = namgun, THIRD face = namseng. Identity only (hair, clothes, bones); REDRAW as webtoon, never photographic skin. BACKGROUND: big graphic shapes and ink-wash, not a photographed place — two or three flat value planes, splashed sumi ink (pomuk) and dry-brush flying-white at the frame edges, paper grain, the world dissolving into Joseon ink at the margins. LIGHT: ONE hard key; each character's hex lives in that light, never a glow aura. ACTING: big readable manhwa faces. New poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NOT photoreal, NOT oil-portrait, NOT live-action. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
